'import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib as mpl

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. COPY POWER BI DATA
# ------------------------------------------------------------

df = dataset.copy()
df.columns = [str(column) for column in df.columns]

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. DEFINE FIELDS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

date_field = "date"
alcohol_field = "alcohol_consumption_count"

preferred_metrics = [
    "sleep_hours",
    "sleep_deep_hours",
    "sleep_rem_hours",
    "hrv_ms",
    "heart_rate_avg",
    "wrist_temperature_f",
    "blood_oxygen_pct",
    "active_energy_kcal",
    "steps",
    "workout_minutes"
]

label_map = {
    "sleep_hours": "Next-Day Sleep",
    "sleep_deep_hours": "Next-Day Deep Sleep",
    "sleep_rem_hours": "Next-Day REM Sleep",
    "hrv_ms": "Next-Day HRV",
    "heart_rate_avg": "Next-Day Average HR",
    "wrist_temperature_f": "Next-Day Wrist Temp",
    "blood_oxygen_pct": "Next-Day Blood Oxygen",
    "active_energy_kcal": "Next-Day Active Energy",
    "steps": "Next-Day Steps",
    "workout_minutes": "Next-Day Workout Min"
}

column_lookup = {
    column.lower(): column
    for column in df.columns
}

if date_field not in column_lookup:
    raise ValueError("date is missing from the visual.")

if alcohol_field not in column_lookup:
    raise ValueError("alcohol_consumption_count is missing from the visual.")

actual_date_field = column_lookup[date_field]
actual_alcohol_field = column_lookup[alcohol_field]

available_metrics = [
    column_lookup[metric]
    for metric in preferred_metrics
    if metric in column_lookup
]

if len(available_metrics) == 0:
    raise ValueError("No usable outcome metrics were found.")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. CLEAN TYPES
# ------------------------------------------------------------

df[actual_date_field] = pd.to_datetime(df[actual_date_field], errors="coerce")
df[actual_alcohol_field] = pd.to_numeric(df[actual_alcohol_field], errors="coerce")

for metric in available_metrics:
    df[metric] = pd.to_numeric(df[metric], errors="coerce")

df = df.dropna(subset=[actual_date_field, actual_alcohol_field]).copy()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. BUILD NEXT-DAY DATASET
#    Match today''s drinks to tomorrow''s metrics
# ------------------------------------------------------------

left_df = df[[actual_date_field, actual_alcohol_field]].copy()
left_df["next_date"] = left_df[actual_date_field] + pd.Timedelta(days=1)

right_df = df[[actual_date_field] + available_metrics].copy()
right_df = right_df.rename(columns={actual_date_field: "next_date"})

next_day_metric_names = {}
for metric in available_metrics:
    new_name = f"next_day__{metric}"
    next_day_metric_names[metric] = new_name

right_df = right_df.rename(columns=next_day_metric_names)

analysis_df = left_df.merge(right_df, on="next_date", how="left")

next_day_metric_columns = list(next_day_metric_names.values())

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. CALCULATE CORRELATIONS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

correlation_matrix = analysis_df[
    [actual_alcohol_field] + next_day_metric_columns
].corr(method="pearson", min_periods=7)

alcohol_correlations = (
    correlation_matrix[actual_alcohol_field]
    .drop(actual_alcohol_field)
    .dropna()
)

if alcohol_correlations.empty:
    raise ValueError("Not enough paired next-day observations to calculate correlations.")

# Count valid paired observations
valid_counts = {}
for metric in next_day_metric_columns:
    valid_counts[metric] = (
        analysis_df[[actual_alcohol_field, metric]]
        .dropna()
        .shape[0]
    )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. PREP DISPLAY DATA
# ------------------------------------------------------------

reverse_metric_lookup = {
    v: k for k, v in next_day_metric_names.items()
}

result = pd.DataFrame({
    "metric": alcohol_correlations.index,
    "correlation": alcohol_correlations.values
})

result["base_metric"] = result["metric"].map(reverse_metric_lookup)

result["label"] = result["base_metric"].apply(
    lambda metric: label_map.get(
        str(metric).lower(),
        str(metric).replace("_", " ").title()
    )
)

result["observations"] = result["metric"].map(valid_counts)

result = result.sort_values("correlation", ascending=True).reset_index(drop=True)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. CREATE BAR CHART
# ------------------------------------------------------------

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(30, 7), dpi=140)

values = result["correlation"].values

normalizer = mpl.colors.Normalize(vmin=-1, vmax=1)
color_map = plt.get_cmap("RdBu_r")

bar_colors = [color_map(normalizer(value)) for value in values]

bars = ax.barh(
    result["label"],
    values,
    color=bar_colors,
    height=0.68
)

ax.axvline(0, color="#333333", linewidth=1.2)

# Value labels
for bar, value in zip(bars, result["correlation"]):
    if value >= 0:
        label_x = value + 0.015
        alignment = "left"
    else:
        label_x = value - 0.015
        alignment = "right"

    ax.text(
        label_x,
        bar.get_y() + bar.get_height() / 2,
        f"{value:+.2f}",
        va="center",
        ha=alignment,
        fontsize=10,
        fontweight="bold"
    )

largest_value = max(
    abs(result["correlation"].min()),
    abs(result["correlation"].max())
)

axis_limit = min(1, max(0.35, largest_value + 0.12))

ax.set_xlim(-axis_limit, axis_limit)

ax.set_xlabel(
    "Pearson correlation with number of drinks today",
    fontsize=10
)

ax.set_ylabel("")

ax.set_title(
    "How Today''s Drinking Relates to Tomorrow''s Health Metrics",
    fontsize=16,
    fontweight="bold",
    pad=16
)

ax.grid(axis="x", linestyle="--", linewidth=0.7, alpha=0.35)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)

for spine in ["top", "right", "left"]:
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)

ax.tick_params(axis="y", length=0, labelsize=10)

fig.text(
    0.5,
    0.01,
    "Negative values mean the next-day metric tends to fall as drinks increase; positive values mean it tends to rise.",
    ha="center",
    fontsize=9
)

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.04, 1, 1])
plt.show()'
